title: Can the iOS 16.5 graphics stack present a first frame without a full GPU driver? Host analysis of the real backboardd/QuartzCore/IOMobileFramebuffer/IOSurface client code from the IPSW (shared cache + binaries) after IOS-005: what happens when no IOAccelerator service matches, which user-client selectors backboardd needs from IOMobileFramebuffer and IOSurface to commit a frame, whether CoreAnimation has a CPU renderer path in 16.5 and what selects it. No promise of software rendering until a run proves it.
acceptance: The note separates (a) what the real 16.5 binaries show (selector numbers, class and service-name strings, control flow around a failed accelerator match, quoted by address and image hash) from (b) donor claims (ios-apollo sweetgl=0 software path; y2sios GPU stack) from (c) unknown.

It states the minimal IOMFB/IOSurface contract needed to commit one frame and compares it with MiniIOMobileFramebuffer/MiniIOSurface in the project kernel, row by row, in the five-word vocabulary of IOS-003 (no row says compatible from a symbol name).

It ends with a decision: either a defined first-frame experiment (question, observable, pass/fail rule) for a later native run, or the statement that a GPU path is on the critical chain, with the minimal GPU work it implies.
steps: Locate the client code in the shared cache
